title: Support constructing AsyncValueRef from std::shared_ptr.
body:
Support constructing AsyncValueRef from std::shared_ptr.

Add an overload `MakeAvailableAsyncValueRef(std::shared_ptr<T> value)` that constructs an available `AsyncValueRef<T>` backed by a `std::shared_ptr<T>`.

When working with APIs that manage object lifetimes via `std::shared_ptr<T>`, wrapping `std::shared_ptr<T>` in `AsyncValueRef<std::shared_ptr<T>>` prevents polymorphic conversion (e.g. `AsyncValueRef<std::shared_ptr<Derived>>` does not convert to `AsyncValueRef<std::shared_ptr<Base>>`). This new API returns an `AsyncValueRef<T>` directly, allowing standard polymorphic conversion (`AsyncValueRef<Derived>` to `AsyncValueRef<Base>`) while sharing ownership with the underlying `std::shared_ptr`.

Under the hood, this introduces `AsyncValue::Kind::kSharedPtr` and `tsl::internal::SharedPtrAsyncValue` to hold `void* ptr_` and `std::shared_ptr<const void> owner_`, providing a single compact 40-byte allocation with zero size overhead for existing `AsyncValue` types.

title: Add CUDA 13 / Blackwell (sm_100, sm_120) local build support
body:
## Summary

Hermetic `cuda_clang` rejects Blackwell architectures (`sm_100` / `sm_120`) with `unsupported CUDA gpu architecture`, which breaks local CUDA 13 builds for GPUs such as GeForce RTX 50-series.

This change improves the **existing** config path (no new `cuda13_nvcc` alias):

- Document that Blackwell builds should use `--config=cuda13_version` + `--config=cuda_nvcc` (+ `--config=cuda_wheel` for pip packages).
- Keep default `--config=cuda` on **CUDA 12** (`cuda_version` → `cuda12_version`).
- Leave `cuda_clang` compute capabilities free of `sm_100` / `sm_120` so the clang path is unchanged.
- In `./configure`, when the user selects sm_100+ capabilities:
  - default the CUDA device compiler to **nvcc** (not clang);
  - if hermetic CUDA/cuDNN versions are unset, pin CUDA **13.0.0** / cuDNN **9.12.0** (same pins as `cuda13_version`);
  - write `--config=cuda_nvcc` for Blackwell; pre-Blackwell non-clang still writes only `--config=cuda`.
- Clarify the pip wheel analysis error for CUDA 13 / Blackwell.
- Add unit tests for capability parsing, CUDA 12 preservation, CUDA 13 pinning, and recommended wheel flags.

## Example build (Blackwell)

```bash
bazel build \
  --config=cuda \
  --config=cuda13_version \
  --config=cuda_nvcc \
  --config=cuda_wheel \
  //tensorflow/tools/pip_package:wheel
```

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m unittest configure_test.py -v` (20 tests)
- [ ] CI (Kokoro) on this PR
- [ ] Manual: `./configure` with `HERMETIC_CUDA_COMPUTE_CAPABILITIES=sm_80` still defaults toward non-Blackwell / CUDA 12 behavior
- [ ] Manual: `./configure` with `sm_120` defaults to nvcc and pins CUDA 13 when versions are left empty
author: tbhaxor

review_comments.body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The conditional checks for the length of `digits` can be simplified. Since the minor version in CUDA compute capabilities is always represented by the last digit (e.g., `sm_90` -> `(9, 0)`, `sm_100` -> `(10, 0)`, `sm_120` -> `(12, 0)`), we can slice the string directly using `digits[:-1]` for the major version and `digits[-1]` for the minor version. This avoids multiple conditional branches and makes the code more concise and maintainable.

```python
    return int(digits[:-1]), int(digits[-1])
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

If the user has explicitly set `HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION` but not `HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION`, the script will only pin `HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION`. However, the printed message will still claim that it is pinning both `HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION` and `HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION` to their Blackwell defaults. We should track which variables are actually pinned and adjust the printed message accordingly to avoid misleading the user.

```python
  pinned_cuda = False
  pinned_cudnn = False
  if not environ_cp.get('HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION'):
    environ_cp['HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION'] = _BLACKWELL_HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION
    write_repo_env_to_bazelrc(
        'cuda', 'HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION', _BLACKWELL_HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION
    )
    pinned_cuda = True
  if not environ_cp.get('HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION'):
    environ_cp['HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION'] = _BLACKWELL_HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION
    write_repo_env_to_bazelrc(
        'cuda', 'HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION', _BLACKWELL_HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION
    )
    pinned_cudnn = True

  if pinned_cuda or pinned_cudnn:
    pins = []
    if pinned_cuda:
      pins.append('HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION=%s' % _BLACKWELL_HERMETIC_CUDA_VERSION)
    if pinned_cudnn:
      pins.append('HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION=%s' % _BLACKWELL_HERMETIC_CUDNN_VERSION)
    print(
        '\nNOTE: Blackwell compute capabilities (sm_100+) selected without an '
        'explicit hermetic CUDA/cuDNN version. Pinning %s. '
        'Default --config=cuda remains CUDA 12 for other builds.\n'
        % ' and '.join(pins)
    )
  return pinned_cuda or pinned_cudnn
```

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for Blackwell GPUs (sm_100 and compute_120) by defaulting to nvcc and pinning hermetic CUDA 13 when Blackwell architectures are selected. It updates .bazelrc configurations, adds helper functions and interactive prompt logic in configure.py, includes comprehensive unit tests in configure_test.py, and updates relevant documentation and wheel build rules. The review feedback suggests simplifying the parsing of CUDA compute capability versions in configure.py and correcting a potentially misleading console message when only one of the hermetic CUDA or cuDNN versions is pinned.

title: [XLA:CPU] Route dot-rooted fusions to MLIR emitter; wrap transpose and DUS
body:
[XLA:CPU] Route dot-rooted fusions to MLIR emitter; wrap transpose and DUS

Three changes toward retiring the legacy LLVM loop emitter:

1. Refactor FusionRoutesToMlirEmitter to a standalone function and remove the kDot
   root exclusion. Unfusing dot fusions instead was measured and
   rejected: it materializes the larger operand (71 ms/call on the
   gemma3-1b copy_dot_fusion, +37% end to end). Routing the fusion to
   the MLIR emitter costs 6.7 ms/call against under 6 for the legacy
   elemental dot (about 2 to 4% end to end on gemma3-1b); max relative
   output difference 7e-7 (reassociation).

2. Wrap standalone transpose and dynamic-update-slice in FusionWrapper and
   clean up legacy standalone dynamic-update-slice thunk & ir_emitter2 handlers.
   MLIR transpose is 1.7x to 2.1x faster than ElementalKernelEmitter
   (f32/bf16 2048x2048, bitwise equal). Dynamic-update-slice is at
   parity with the IrEmitter2 in-place kernel (bitwise equal).

3. Add a VLOG probe on the remaining legacy fusion route so corpus
   scans can attribute every remaining use.

title: PR #46097: [xla:gpu] Add collective_group_key frontend attribute and honor it as a collective-combining boundary
body:
PR #46097: [xla:gpu] Add collective_group_key frontend attribute and honor it as a collective-combining boundary

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46097

This PR introduces a `collective_group_key` frontend attribute that lets a frontend mark independent collectives (all-gather, all-reduce, reduce-scatter, collective-permute) that should be launched and scheduled together as one group. The key acts as a **combining boundary**: transformations that coalesce two *distinct* collectives must not merge a keyed collective with an unannotated one or with one carrying a different key.

The main part is this change: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46097/changes#diff-1a61849fd610e8963dd436981558524ae241f7bbda1ca5e8da5dd70d6b2b86ccR118 (changes in xla/side_effect_util.h documenting attr sematnics)

### Motivation

We want to stop XLA from combining collectives from unrelated layers (i.e. if we unroll a loop in python), and instead allow grouping different collectives together as a group, i.e. we can execute `all-gather` and `collective-permute` inside a single collective group (XLA runtime already supports it).

### Semantics

  - **Combining is constrained.** Merging two distinct collectives (combiners, reassociation, and the collective-permute / all-gather-optimizer coalescers) requires compatible group keys.
  - **CSE, decomposition, splitting, and movement are not.** These may proceed; the key is forwarded onto the rewritten op, preserved when there is one unambiguous representative, or cleared when representatives conflict.
  - Because moved members may land in different computations and stop grouping, frontends must use a module-wide-unique key per logical group.

### Changes

  **Attribute contract** (`side_effect_util`, `collective_ops_utils`)
  - Add `collective_group_key`, and document `combiner_key` alongside it with clearly distinct roles: `collective_group_key` requests a launch group and constrains cross-collective combining; `combiner_key` only partitions same-type combining.
  - Add helpers: `GetCollectiveGroupKey`, `HasCollectiveGroupKey`, `HaveCompatibleCollectiveGroupKeys` (empty matches only empty), and `CopyCollectiveGroupKey` / `ClearCollectiveGroupKey` for forwarding the key through rewrites.

  **Combining boundaries**
  - Combiners (all-gather / all-reduce / reduce-scatter): frontend attributes are folded into the combiner group key via a length-prefixed encoding (`AppendFrontendAttributesToCombinerKey`), so arbitrary frontend strings cannot produce colliding keys.
  - `MergeCollectiveBackendConfig` now OR-merges both `is_pipelined` and `is_spmd_generated`.
  - All-reduce and reduce-scatter reassociation and schedule-aware collective CSE require compatible group keys.
  - Collective-permute combining: `CollectivePermuteKey` now includes `collective_group_key` (and `combiner_key`).
  - `AllGatherOptimizer` additionally checks backend-config compatibility before coalescing two all-gathers and merges configs into the result.

  **Key forwarding through non-combining rewrites**
  - `AllReduceFolder` folds keyed chains, preserving a unique representative key and dropping conflicting ones instead of synthesizing a composite key.
  - `AllReduceSplitter`, `AllReduceDecomposer`, `AllReduceContiguous`, `ReduceScatterCreator`, `WhileLoopAllReduceCodeMotion`, `CollectivePipeliner`, and the all-gather pad/permuted-DS simplifiers now use `SetupDerivedInstruction` / `CopyCollectiveGroupKey` / `ClearCollectiveGroupKey` so the attribute is correctly propagated (or intentionally cleared) onto rewritten collectives.

title: PR #46077: Add CUPTI 13.3 multi-subscriber support with 13.2 fallback
body:
PR #46077: Add CUPTI 13.3 multi-subscriber support with 13.2 fallback

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46077

📝 Summary of Changes
  - Added CUPTI V2 multi-subscriber support for CUPTI 13.3, using a fresh subscriber for each profiling
    session.
  - Used subscriber-scoped V2 APIs for timestamps and activity processing.
  - Kept each subscriber alive until its cached activity buffers were processed.
  - Preserved the legacy V1 path when V2 support is unavailable.

🎯 Justification
  This enables CUPTI V2 multi-subscriber support for CUPTI 13.3. It allows XLA to create an independent
  subscriber for each profiling session and lays the groundwork for using PGLE alongside NVIDIA Nsight Systems.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
   🐛 Bug Fix, ✨ New Feature, ♻️ Cleanup, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Not applicable. This change does not introduce a performance optimization.

🧪 Unit Tests:
  Added cupti_tracer_test coverage for:
  - V2 subscribe failures falling back to V1
  - V2 timestamp failures after subscription falling back to V1
  - Fatal initial V2 timestamp failures without duplicate unsubscribe
  - Preparing a fresh V2 subscriber for each profiling session
  - Fatal stop-timestamp failures without duplicate unsubscribe

  Expanded cupti_error_manager_test coverage for:
  - Nonfatal V2 activity-configuration errors
  - Nonfatal V2 activity-record errors without falling back to the V1 parser

  These tests cover V2 capability detection, V1 fallback, fresh subscribers across sessions, subscriber-scoped  timestamps, V2 activity-record handling, and cleanup after fatal errors.

🧪 Execution Tests:
  No new dedicated execution test was added.
  The existing end-to-end JAX GPU profiling tests passed using both the V1 path such as CUPTI 12.9 and the V2 path with
  CUPTI 13.3:
  - JAX //tests:pgle_test_gpu: passed
  - JAX //tests:profiler_test_gpu: passed

title: PR #45950: [XLA:GPU] Do not fuse a slice onto a costly-to-duplicate operand.
body:
PR #45950: [XLA:GPU] Do not fuse a slice onto a costly-to-duplicate operand.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45950

📝 Summary of Changes
Adds an `IsCheapToDuplicate` operand check to the slice-fusion path in `IsInputWorthFusing`. A slice reaching a producer shared by multiple consumers (through single-user reshapes/bitcasts/transposes) is now fused only if that producer is cheap to duplicate. Otherwise, e.g., a dynamic-slice reached through a reshape, as in paligemma, are left unfused.

🎯 Justification
Commit ac6958edf3 caused a ~6% regression in paligemma inference. This restores it.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, ⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
paligemma inference 1 GPU MI350X, 23.43 ms → 22.07 ms (−5.8%)

🧪 Unit Tests:
`IsInputWorthFusingSliceNotWorthThroughSharedNonElementwiseOperand`
Copybara import of the project:

ac6958edf3 regressed paligemma ~7%. The shared MLP-weight dynamic-slice

Gate the branch on IsCheapToDuplicate(operand) so only the cheap cases fuse.

title: Add global positive-dimension shape product validation to TFLite verifier.
body:
Add global positive-dimension shape product validation to TFLite verifier.

title: PR #46026: [XLA:GPU] Lower scaled-dot operand transposes in XTile-to-Triton
body:
PR #46026: [XLA:GPU] Lower scaled-dot operand transposes in XTile-to-Triton

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46026

📝 Summary of Changes
- Lower transposes created during XTile scaled-dot canonicalization to `tt.trans`. The transpose lowering is shared between the StableHLO-to-Triton and XTile-to-Triton passes.
- Canonicalize scaled-dot result shapes by collapsing unit dimensions to the 2D shape required by Triton.

This is another PR in the scaled dot fix series (part of https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44223).

🎯 Justification

Canonicalizing a scaled dot can create `stablehlo.transpose`. Previously, these operations can be created after the StableHLO-to-Triton pass and remain in the IR. This prevents the XTile-to-Triton pipeline from fully lowering MXFP4 scaled dots. Registering transpose lowering in the XTile-to-Triton pass produces the expected Triton IR. This mirrors the existing LowerReshape handling: operand canonicalization can create both reshapes and transposes after StableHLO-to-Triton lowering, so both rewrites must also run in the XTile-to-Triton pass.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

🧪 Unit Tests:
New test TritonScaledDotTest.Mxfp4KPackedRhsSm120Executes
Without this fix, it fails because the generated IR retains `stablehlo.transpose`.

body:
Fix MSVC compilation error in LiteRT kernels.

Move preprocessor directives out of `TF_LITE_ENSURE` macro arguments in `dequantize.cc`, `split.cc`, and `split_v.cc`.

title: Fix CublasLt vector bias epilogue fusion: alpha * (A@B + bias).
body:
Fix CublasLt vector bias epilogue fusion: alpha * (A@B + bias).

"Default" CublasLt gemms are defined as alpha * (A@B) + beta * bias, but require A, B and C to be matrices (not vectors). 

In the case of the bias being a vector CublasLt offers a special epilogue fusion for vector bias. In this case we do not have a "default" cublas gemm but a "BIAS" cublas gemm. Note that for a BIAS gemm we set beta to 0. Also note we will emit the bias by setting CUBLASLT_MATMUL_DESC_BIAS_POINTER in cublasLtMatmulDesc_t (see https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cublas/index.html#cublasltmatmuldesc-t).

When handling the multiply op we would remove the multiply op effectively calculating alpha * (A@B) + bias instead of the correct alpha * (A@B + bias). We should only remove the multiply op if we have a default CublasLt gemm.

Related: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/39336

title: PR #44796: SPMD: Use collective-broadcast for replicated dynamic-slice from sharded operands
body:
PR #44796: SPMD: Use collective-broadcast for replicated dynamic-slice from sharded operands

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44796

## Summary

This PR adds an SPMD lowering for a dynamic-slice pattern that appears in the Layered-FSDP forward pass for Muon workloads.

When a replicated result dynamically slices a single layer from an operand sharded along the layer dimension, XLA previously materialized the full operand with an all-gather and then sliced out the requested layer. This PR lowers that pattern to a per-owner `collective-broadcast`: each partition slices its local candidate, a conditional selects the partition that owns the requested layer, and that owner broadcasts only the selected slice.

## Workload

The motivating workload is Layered-FSDP for Muon.

Muon's Newton-Schulz update needs the full weight/gradient matrix for each layer. To preserve full matrices locally, Layered-FSDP shards scanned layer stacks along the layer dimension instead of sharding the matrix row/column dimensions.

A representative weight layout is:

```text
logical shape: [L, K, N]
sharding:      P("lp", None, None)
```

where `L` is the scanned layer dimension and `lp` is the layer-parallel mesh axis.

During the forward pass, the scan body selects the current layer:

```text
W_i = dynamic-slice(W, i, 0, 0), dynamic_slice_sizes={1, K, N}
```

The selected `W_i` is needed replicated across the LP partitions for the layer computation. If `L == LP`, layer `i` is owned by LP partition `i`.

The ideal communication pattern for scan iteration `i` is therefore:

```text
owner = partition that owns layer i
broadcast W_i from owner to all LP partitions
```

## Original Issue

Before this PR, XLA SPMD did not have a specialized lowering for this case:

```text
replicated result = dynamic-slice(tiled operand, dynamic layer index)
```

Because the operand is sharded on the sliced dimension but the dynamic-slice result is replicated, the existing path falls back to replicating the operand first. In practice this produces:

```text
all-gather full W across LP
dynamic-slice W_i from the gathered W
```

That is correct, but inefficient for this workload.

For example, if the scan only needs one layer's weight `[1, K, N]`, the old lowering gathers the full layer stack `[L, K, N]` and then slices out one layer. This defeats the purpose of Layered-FSDP's layerwise ownership for the forward pass, because every scan iteration communicates all layer shards instead of the one layer needed by that iteration.

## Solution In This PR

This PR adds `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::TryDynamicSliceWithCollectiveBroadcast` and calls it from `HandleDynamicSlice` before the generic replicated-output fallback.

The new lowering matches a conservative pattern:

```text
- dynamic-slice output is replicated
- operand is tiled
- exactly one dimension is dynamically sliced
- sliced size is 1
- operand is sharded only along the sliced dimension
- no partial replication
- partitioning is even
- slice index is an S32 scalar
- operand sharding uses the same number of devices as the SPMD partition count
```

For the matched case, XLA lowers:

```text
dynamic-slice(tiled_operand, i) -> replicated result
```

to:

```text
clamped_i   = clamp(i, 0, dim_size - 1)
owner       = clamped_i / shard_size
local_i     = clamped_i - owner * shard_size
local_slice = dynamic-slice(local_operand, local_i)

result = conditional(owner)
  branch 0: collective-broadcast(local_slice), root=partition owning shard 0
  branch 1: collective-broadcast(local_slice), root=partition owning shard 1
  ...
```

Each conditional branch contains a `collective-broadcast` with a static root. The dynamic part is only the branch selection, which is derived from the replicated layer index. This lets the HLO represent the desired "changing owner per scan iteration" pattern without requiring a dynamic-root collective.

The generated communication now moves only the selected layer slice instead of all layer shards.

## Before / After

Before:

```text
all-gather W_local -> W_full
dynamic-slice W_full[i]
```

After:

```text
local dynamic-slice W_local[local_i]
conditional(owner)
  collective-broadcast from owner partition
```

So the forward pass communication changes from:

```text
communicate [L, K, N] per scan iteration
```

to:

```text
communicate [1, K, N] per scan iteration
```

for the matched Layered-FSDP pattern.

## Testing

Added a focused SPMD partitioner test:

```text
DynamicSliceReplicatedResultUsesCollectiveBroadcast
```

The test verifies that a replicated dynamic-slice result from a layer-sharded operand produces:

```text
- no all-gather
- one conditional with one branch per owner partition
- collective-broadcast in each branch
- replica groups whose first member is the branch's broadcast root
```

Validation performed for the motivating workload:

```text
bazel test --test_output=errors \
  --test_filter="DynamicSliceReplicatedResultUsesCollectiveBroadcast" \
  //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test
```

Additional workload validation:

```text
- Rebuilt JAX/JAXLIB CUDA artifacts against this XLA checkout.
- Ran lp_fsdp_muon_test.py --mode lp --no-run --dump-hlo with
  JAX_ENABLE_COMPILATION_CACHE=false.
- Confirmed the LP forward HLO contains the expected conditional
  collective-broadcast lowering.
```

Observed HLO counts for the workload:

```text
collective-broadcast-start = 32
collective-broadcast-done  = 32
conditional                = 4
dynamic_slice_collective_broadcast_owner = 16
all-gather-start           = 0
all-gather-done            = 0
```


🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, ⚡️ Performance Improvement, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
No public HLO benchmark result is included. The validation target was the layer-FSDP forward HLO from the muon_jax repro. With a fresh JAX compile, the LP forward HLO has 0 all-gather-start/all-gather-done ops and contains the expected conditional collective-broadcast lowering.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- bazel test --test_output=errors --test_filter="*DynamicSliceReplicatedResultUsesCollectiveBroadcast*" //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test

🧪 Execution Tests:
- Rebuilt JAX/JAXLIB CUDA artifacts against this XLA checkout.
- Ran lp_fsdp_muon_test.py --mode lp --no-run --dump-hlo with JAX_ENABLE_COMPILATION_CACHE=false.
- Confirmed HLO counts: collective-broadcast-start=32, collective-broadcast-done=32, conditional=4, dynamic_slice_collective_broadcast_owner=16, all-gather-start=0, all-gather-done=0.

title: PR #45296: [XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Add GELU_ERF pattern matching for StableHLO legalized erfc
body:
PR #45296: [XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Add GELU_ERF pattern matching for StableHLO legalized erfc

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45296

Expand CPU oneDNN GELU pattern matching to recognize the exact-GELU form emitted by JAX/StableHLO after `erfc` legalization. This handles the piecewise `select(abs(y) < 1, 1 - ..., ...)` structure for `erfc(-x / sqrt(2))`, in addition to the existing `tanh` and `erf` forms. The decomposition happens because exact GELU lowers through `erfc`, and StableHLO legalizes `erfc` into portable primitive ops rather than preserving it as a first-class op. The matcher stays loose on approximation internals and instead matches the stable mathematical skeleton, improving fusion robustness for Keras/JAX workloads.

title: [XLA:GPU] Fix convolution padding legalization for convolution fusions.
body:
[XLA:GPU] Fix convolution padding legalization for convolution fusions.

Conv padding legalization makes the low and high padding symmetric, e.g. padding 1_2 becomes padding 1_1 (low_high).

For a DGRAD conv CUDNN custom call the padding must be the padding applied to the forward convolution from which the DGRAD conv originated from. E.g. both `Y[2,4,3,3,2] convolution(X, W), pad=2_1x1_1x1_1` and `Y[2,4,3,3,2] cudnn-custom-call(X, W), pad=0_1x1_1x1_1` are the same.

In contrary to ones intuition lowering the padding from 1_2 to 1_1 actually increases the output dimension of a cudnn DGRAD conv. E.g. `Y[2,4,3,3,2] cudnn-custom-call(X, W), pad=0_1x1_1x1_1`becomes `Y[2,**5**,3,3,2] cudnn-custom-call(X, W), pad=0_**0**x1_1x1_1`. 

This is NOT the case for raw covolution ops, where an increase in padding results in an increase in output dimension size. E.g. `Y[2,4,3,3,2] convolution(X, W), pad=2_1x1_1x1_1` would become `Y[2,5,3,3,2] convolution(X, W), pad=2_2x1_1x1_1`

title: PR #45938: [XLA:GPU] Simplify DeviceAddressVmmAllocator mapped Allocate() API
body:
PR #45938: [XLA:GPU] Simplify DeviceAddressVmmAllocator mapped Allocate() API

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45938

## Summary

Removes the `return_reservation_address=false` mode from `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator`'s mapped `Allocate()` overload and drops the `return_reservation_address` parameter entirely. There is no use case for the mode that returned a separate allocator-owned address alongside a reservation-address alias, so the mapped `Allocate()` now always returns the mapped reservation slice as the allocator address:

```cpp
absl::StatusOr<ScopedDeviceAddress<uint8_t>> Allocate(
    int device_ordinal, uint64_t allocation_size, bool retry_on_failure,
    int64_t memory_space, MemoryReservation* reservation,
    uint64_t reservation_offset, uint64_t mapping_size);
```

## Details

- Removed the `MappedAddressMode` enum and the `mode` field of `MappedAllocateRequest`.
- Collapsed `AllocationRecord::Kind::{kAllocateAndMapReturnMapAddr, kAllocateAndMapReturnNewAddr}` into a single `kAllocateAndMap`.
- `TryReuseMappedAllocation()` and `CreateMappedAllocation()` lost their separate-address branches (no allocator-owned reservation creation, alias installation, or dual pending-entry handling in the mapped path).
- Reservation-address aliases are now created only by `Map()`; class docs (address-behavior table, API flows, `Deallocate`/`Map`/`UnMap` contracts) and error messages updated accordingly.
- Updated the single production call site in `gpu_executable_va_remap_allocator.cc`.
- Deleted the two CUDA tests that existed solely for the removed mode; other call sites just drop the argument.

Net: **−188 lines**.

## Testing

- `bazel build --config=cuda` of `//xla/stream_executor:device_address_vmm_allocator{,_test}`, `//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_buffer_allocator`, and `//xla/stream_executor/cuda:cuda_device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: success.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: 4/4 passed.
- `cuda_device_address_vmm_allocator_test` (H200): 31/31 passed.

title: Validate updates rank in TensorScatter ops to prevent CHECK failure crash
body:
Fixes #94132.

`TensorScatterOp::Compute()` (backs `TensorScatterUpdate`/`Add`/`Sub`/`Min`/`Max`) computes `outer_dims = indices.shape().dims() - 1`, then loops over `outer_dims` calling `updates.shape().dim_size(i)` without checking that `updates` actually has that many dimensions. A malformed indices/updates pair (e.g. indices rank 3, updates rank 1) hits a fatal `CHECK failed: d < dims()` instead of a normal error.

Added a rank check before the loop, same `OP_REQUIRES`/`InvalidArgumentError` style already used for the indices/updates rank-at-least-one checks a few lines above. Added `testUpdateMinUpdatesRankTooLow` in the existing `ScatterNdTensorTest` class, matching this file's own `assertRaisesWithPredicateMatch` convention for invalid-shape tests.

Verified with `bazel test //tensorflow/python/kernel_tests/array_ops:scatter_nd_ops_test --test_filter=ScatterNdTensorTest.testUpdateMinUpdatesRankTooLow` (CPU and GPU variants both pass).
author: somtri

review_comments.body:
![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

There is a minor formatting inconsistency in the error message. The label `Indices shape: ` has a trailing space, but `, updates shape:` is missing one. Adding a space after the colon improves the readability of the error message.

```c
    OP_REQUIRES(c, updates.shape().dims() >= outer_dims,
                absl::InvalidArgumentError(absl::StrCat(
                    "Updates must have rank of at least ", outer_dims,
                    " to match the outer dimensions of indices. Indices "
                    "shape: ",
                    indices.shape().DebugString(),
                    ", updates shape: ", updates.shape().DebugString())));
```

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces a validation check in TensorScatterOp to ensure that the rank of updates is at least equal to the outer dimensions of indices, preventing a fatal crash and raising an InvalidArgumentError instead. A regression test is also added to verify this behavior. The review feedback points out a minor formatting inconsistency in the error message string, suggesting the addition of a missing space for better readability.

### Review of Pull Request

Thank you for the contribution. The fix correctly addresses a potential crash in `TensorScatterOp::Compute` when `updates` has a lower rank than expected based on `indices`.

#### Further Audit

Following the logic, similar scatter operations were audited:

1. **`ScatterNd` (`ScatterNdOp::Compute`)**: This operation shares the exact same validation logic and loop structure. It is **also vulnerable** to this crash scenario (a `CHECK` failure/abort when `updates` rank is lower than `outer_dims`).
2. **`ScatterNdUpdate` (`ScatterNdUpdateOp::DoCompute`)**: This operation delegates validation to `ValidateScatterNdUpdateShape` before performing similar checks, and thus is protected.

#### Recommendations

It is highly recommended to apply this exact same fix to `ScatterNd` as well, as it suffers from the same vulnerability. The fix can be placed in `ScatterNdOp::Compute` just before the dimension matching loop.

#### Test Cases

Here are unit tests that reproduce the crash scenario. They should pass (raise `InvalidArgumentError`) with the fix applied, but would crash/abort without it.

##### For `tensor_scatter_nd_update` (Verifies your fix):

```python
def testUpdateMinUpdatesRankTooLow(self):
    indices = tf.constant([[[0]], [[0]]], dtype=tf.int32) # shape [2, 1, 1], rank 3
    updates = tf.constant([1.0, 2.0], dtype=tf.float32) # shape [2], rank 1
    t = tf.ones([1], dtype=tf.float32)
    with self.assertRaises((tf.errors.InvalidArgumentError, ValueError)):
        tf.tensor_scatter_nd_update(t, indices, updates)
```

##### For `scatter_nd` (Recommends extending the fix):

```python
def testScatterNdMinUpdatesRankTooLow(self):
    indices = tf.constant([[[0]], [[0]]], dtype=tf.int32) # shape [2, 1, 1], rank 3
    updates = tf.constant([1.0, 2.0], dtype=tf.float32) # shape [2], rank 1
    shape = [1]
    with self.assertRaises((tf.errors.InvalidArgumentError, ValueError)):
        tf.scatter_nd(indices, updates, shape)
```

Adding these tests ensures comprehensive coverage and prevents regressions in both ops.

commit_messages:
Validate updates rank in TensorScatter ops to prevent CHECK failure crash

Fixes #94132.

TensorScatterOp::Compute() (backs TensorScatterUpdate/Add/Sub/Min/Max)
computes outer_dims = indices.shape().dims() - 1, then loops over
outer_dims calling updates.shape().dim_size(i) without checking that
updates actually has that many dimensions. A malformed indices/updates
pair (e.g. indices rank 3, updates rank 1) hits a fatal
CHECK failed: d < dims() instead of a normal error.

Added a rank check before the loop, same OP_REQUIRES/InvalidArgumentError
style already used for the indices/updates rank-at-least-one checks a few
lines above. Added testUpdateMinUpdatesRankTooLow in the existing
ScatterNdTensorTest class, matching this file's own
assertRaisesWithPredicateMatch convention for invalid-shape tests.

Verified with bazel test
//tensorflow/python/kernel_tests/array_ops:scatter_nd_ops_test
--test_filter=ScatterNdTensorTest.testUpdateMinUpdatesRankTooLow
(CPU and GPU variants both pass).

title: PR #45673: [ROCm] Handle singleton tile dims in TDM lowering
body:
PR #45673: [ROCm] Handle singleton tile dims in TDM lowering

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45673

📝 Summary of Changes
Makes AMD TDM lowering correctly handle operand tiles that carry a size-1
(singleton) dimension. Singleton dims are folded into the descriptor base
pointer to build a reduced-rank descriptor when safe, otherwise TDM is declined.

🎯 Justification
Batched GEMMs and scaled dots on gfx1250 reach this lowering with singleton 
batch tiles. Previously they were either needlessly rejected or lowered to a 
malformed TDM descriptor. This makes them use the TDM path where valid 
and fall back safely where not.

🚀 Kind of Contribution 🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:
New test in in triton_xla_extract_insert_to_triton.mlir and triton_pipeline_tdm.mlir.

🧪 Execution Tests:
New tests in triton_gemm_fusion_test.cc
Copybara import of the project:

--
4adfec5c8c69eaadb88a0fc5d3a66ad2c76e00cb by Aleksei Nurmukhametov <anurmukh@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Handle singleton tile dims in TDM lowering

A tile can reach the extract/insert lowering with a size-1 dim at any
position, e.g. when a dot with batch dims is tiled one batch per program.
The TDM path handled these incorrectly. Fix it in two parts:

1. When the surviving minor-most dim has global stride 1, fold the
   singleton tile dims (at any position) into the descriptor base pointer
   and build a reduced-rank descriptor from the survivors, so no size-1
   dim is left in the descriptor. Previously these tiles were rejected
   and fell back to plain load/store.

2. Otherwise skip TDM and fall back to plain load/store. Folding cannot
   help: the surviving minor-most dim inherits a non-unit stride that a
   TDM descriptor cannot express. Previously such a tile kept its size-1
   dim in the descriptor and either read the wrong memory or failed
   Triton legalization:

     error: requires shared order [rank-1, rank-2, ..., 0]
     error: failed to legalize operation 'tt.make_tensor_descriptor' ...

   Also skip when that dim spans fewer than 2 dwords, e.g. an f8 operand
   with a size-4 minor dim. It is a TDM pad interval limitation.

The TDM-specific helpers are extracted into tdm_lowering_util.{h,cc},
with the shared layout utilities moved to lowering_util.{h.cc}.

Merging this change closes #45673

title: PR #45871: [HLO] Validate operand count and shape in recv/conditional/rng-bit-generator/reduce-window parsing
body:
PR #45871: [HLO] Validate operand count and shape in recv/conditional/rng-bit-generator/reduce-window parsing

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45871

### Problem
Four opcode handlers in `HloParserImpl::CreateInstruction` read a parsed operand or the result shape without validating it, so malformed-but-lexable HLO aborts the parser (a `CHECK` failure or an out-of-bounds read) instead of returning an error `Status`:

- **`recv`** — `CreateRecv(shape->tuple_shapes(0), ...)` calls `tuple_shapes(0)` without checking the result shape is a non-empty tuple, so a non-tuple shape `CHECK`-fails in `Shape::tuple_state()`:
  ```
  tok = token[] after-all()
  ROOT recv = f32[10] recv(tok)
  ```
- **`conditional`** — reads `operands[0]->shape()` immediately after a count-agnostic `ParseOperands`, so zero operands reads past the end (the later count check is downstream):
  ```
  ROOT c = f32[] conditional()
  ```
- **`rng-bit-generator`** — reads `operands[0]` after a count-agnostic `ParseOperands`:
  ```
  ROOT r = (u64[2], u32[4]) rng-bit-generator(), algorithm=rng_three_fry
  ```
- **`reduce-window`** — its operand-count check only rejects an *odd* count, so zero operands passes and the shape-inference lambda reads `operands[0]`/`operands[1]`:
  ```
  ROOT rw = reduce-window(), to_apply=add
  ```

### Fix
- `recv`: guard `!shape->IsTuple() || shape->tuple_shapes().empty()` before `tuple_shapes(0)`, mirroring the existing `kInfeed` guard.
- `conditional`, `reduce-window`: return a parse error when `operands` is empty.
- `rng-bit-generator`: pass `ParseOperands(..., /*expected_size=*/1)`.

### Tests
Four `HloParserTest` cases assert these malformed inputs now return an error instead of crashing.

---
Disclosure: this contribution was authored with an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed before submission.

title: PR #45877: [XLA:GPU][oneAPI/SPIR-V] Skip compilation and loading of empty constants modules
body: PR #45877: [XLA:GPU][oneAPI/SPIR-V] Skip compilation and loading of empty constants modules Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45877 Hello, xla and intel team, in my journey to understand and improve the SPIR-V compilation pipeline in PJRT, I found that XLA always passes the constants LLVM module to the target compiler, even when the module is empty. I observed 2 time the `oneAPI::zeModuleCreate_SPIRVToNative` function being called, once for the kernel and once for the empty constants module. This can be seen by a [perfetto](https://perfetto.dev/) screenshot. I think the empty constants module can be skipped entirely, avoiding unnecessary compilation and module loading. ## 📝 Summary of Changes * Skip target-binary compilation when the emitted constants LLVM module contains no functions or globals. * Skip device-module loading whenever the constants binary is empty, instead of handling this case only for CUDA. * Verify that constants metadata is not present without a corresponding constants binary. * Add a regression test covering resolution of an empty constants binary. ## 🎯 Justification Previously, XLA always passed the constants LLVM module to the target compiler, even when the module was empty. \ At runtime, loading an empty constants module was skipped only for CUDA. This unnecessarily requires other GPU backends to support compilation and loading of empty modules. \ In particular, it blocks SPIR-V-oriented GPU compilation paths for HLO modules that do not emit device constants. The change makes the empty-constants case platform-independent. Constant-free GPU workloads benefit from avoiding an invalid or unnecessary constants compilation and module-loading step. ## 🚀 Kind of Contribution 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests ## 📊 Benchmark This is mainly a correctness and backend-portability fix, but the purpose is to avoid unnecessary compilation and module loading for empty constants modules so it may improve performance in such cases. ## 🧪 Unit Tests Added `GpuModuleGlobalsTest.EmptyBinarySkipsModuleLoading` to `gpu_executable_test.cc`. The test uses mock stream and stream-executor objects to verify that resolving an empty constants binary: * does not query the platform; * does not call `LoadModule`; and * returns an empty globals map. Test target: ```bash export ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0 bazel test //xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_test \ --test_filter=GpuModuleGlobalsTest.EmptyBinarySkipsModuleLoading ``` ```bash bazel build //xla/pjrt/c:pjrt_c_api_gpu_plugin.so \ --config=sycl_hermetic \ --repo_env=ONEAPI_VERSION=2026.0 \ --repo_env=OS=ubuntu_24.10 ``` ## 🧪 Execution Tests None added. The changed behavior concerns empty constants-module handling and is covered by the focused hardware-independent unit test above. Copybara import of the project: -- 03d75a853d5828bbff41d32f15f372329ce5543b by Kevin Barre : [XLA:GPU] Skip compilation and loading of empty constants modules Avoid compiling the constants LLVM module when it contains no functions or global variables. In this case, no target binary is produced. Update GpuModuleGlobals to skip module loading whenever the constants binary is empty, independent of the GPU platform. This prevents backends such as oneAPI from attempting to load an empty module specification. commit_messages: PR #45877: [XLA:GPU][oneAPI/SPIR-V] Skip compilation and loading of empty constants modules Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45877 Hello, xla and intel team, in my journey to understand and improve the SPIR-V compilation pipeline in PJRT, I found that XLA always passes the constants LLVM module to the target compiler, even when the module is empty. I observed 2 time the `oneAPI::zeModuleCreate_SPIRVToNative` function being called, once for the kernel and once for the empty constants module. This can be seen by a [perfetto](https://perfetto.dev/) screenshot. I think the empty constants module can be skipped entirely, avoiding unnecessary compilation and module loading. ## 📝 Summary of Changes * Skip target-binary compilation when the emitted constants LLVM module contains no functions or globals. * Skip device-module loading whenever the constants binary is empty, instead of handling this case only for CUDA. * Verify that constants metadata is not present without a corresponding constants binary. * Add a regression test covering resolution of an empty constants binary. ## 🎯 Justification Previously, XLA always passed the constants LLVM module to the target compiler, even when the module was empty. \ At runtime, loading an empty constants module was skipped only for CUDA. This unnecessarily requires other GPU backends to support compilation and loading of empty modules. \ In particular, it blocks SPIR-V-oriented GPU compilation paths for HLO modules that do not emit device constants. The change makes the empty-constants case platform-independent. Constant-free GPU workloads benefit from avoiding an invalid or unnecessary constants compilation and module-loading step. ## 🚀 Kind of Contribution 🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests ## 📊 Benchmark This is mainly a correctness and backend-portability fix, but the purpose is to avoid unnecessary compilation and module loading for empty constants modules so it may improve performance in such cases. ## 🧪 Unit Tests Added `GpuModuleGlobalsTest.EmptyBinarySkipsModuleLoading` to `gpu_executable_test.cc`. The test uses mock stream and stream-executor objects to verify that resolving an empty constants binary: * does not query the platform; * does not call `LoadModule`; and * returns an empty globals map. Test target: ```bash export ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:0 bazel test //xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_test \ --test_filter=GpuModuleGlobalsTest.EmptyBinarySkipsModuleLoading ``` ```bash bazel build //xla/pjrt/c:pjrt_c_api_gpu_plugin.so \ --config=sycl_hermetic \ --repo_env=ONEAPI_VERSION=2026.0 \ --repo_env=OS=ubuntu_24.10 ``` ## 🧪 Execution Tests None added. The changed behavior concerns empty constants-module handling and is covered by the focused hardware-independent unit test above. title: PR #46018: [ROCm---XLA:GPU] Disable AnnotationStack on GpuTracer::DoStart() failure (ROCm)
body:
PR #46018: [ROCm---XLA:GPU] Disable AnnotationStack on GpuTracer::DoStart() failure (ROCm)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46018

GpuTracer::DoStart() enables AnnotationStack before calling rocm_tracer_->Enable(). If Enable() fails, the previous RETURN_IF_ERROR returned without reversing the Enable(true). GpuTracer::Stop() only calls DoStop() — and thus AnnotationStack::Enable(false) — when profiling_state_ is kStartedOk, so a failed start left the annotation stack permanently enabled for the process lifetime, adding per-call overhead with no profiler running.

Fix: replace RETURN_IF_ERROR with an explicit status check that calls AnnotationStack::Enable(false) before propagating the error, mirroring the same fix applied to CuptiTracer::DoStart() in the preceding commit.

Remove the now-unused status_macros.h include.

title: PR #46043: [xla:gpu] Treat explicit collective groups as GPU async collectives
body:
PR #46043: [xla:gpu] Treat explicit collective groups as GPU async collectives

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46043

Explicit collective groups are represented as generic `async-start`/`async-done` operations annotated with `_collectives_group` attribute, but the GPU backend did not consistently recognize them as collective operations. 

####  This change:

  - Recognizes explicit collective-group start/done operations as GPU async collectives.
  - Assigns them to the collective execution stream and accounts for each group as one collective resource.
  - Preserves opaque resource accounting through nested calls and while loops instead of recursively counting every collective in the group.
  - Collects replica groups from the grouped collectives so rank-overlap scheduling constraints remain enforced.
  - Conservatively serializes groups when replica-group information is implicit or unavailable.
  - Preserves `force_earliest_schedule` on the group start while clearing it on the done operation, allowing latency hiding.
  - Extends scheduling-annotation legalization to look through nested async call-like wrappers.


This makes collective group call a proper first class collective-operation-citizen in XLA GPU runtime.

(while I'm here migrate touched tests away from `TF_ASSERT_OK_AND_ASSIGN`)

title: PR #44560: [ROCm][Triton] All gather thunk dispatch (PR2/4)
body:
PR #44560: [ROCm][Triton] All gather thunk dispatch (PR2/4)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44560

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the second in a series of four.

PR 1/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44559   
PR 2/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44560   <--- This PR
PR 3/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44562
PR 4/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44564

These PRs aim to enable the Triton backend for the All-Gather collective operation based on the experimental tiling strategy.

The PR wires AllGather through CollectiveKernelThunk/AllGatherThunk at runtime, and adds a dedicated flag.

🎯 Justification
Lowering All-Gather through the triton backend significantly improves performance of this operation for AMD/ROCm target (compared to RCCL backend), especially for small tensor, and could allow us to take greater advantage of kernel-level fusion.

Example of 5 Triton Performance Improvements — All-Gather 1D on MI355
 | DType | Shape | Replicas | Triton (µs) | RCCL (µs) | Speedup |
|--------|--------|----------|------------------:|---------------:|--------:|
| s8 | [16384] | 2 | 17.428 | 42.342 | **2.43×** |
| bf16 | [16384] | 2 | 17.708 | 41.733 | **2.36×** |
| f32 | [131072] | 2 | 27.924 | 52.497 | **1.88×** |
| s32 | [4096] | 2 | 24.435 | 44.287 | **1.81×** |
| s8 | [262144] | 4 | 40.459 | 71.119 | **1.76×** |

Example of 5 Triton Performance Improvements — All-Gather 2D on MI355
dtype | shape | replicas | RCCL (µs) | Triton (µs) | speedup
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
bf16 | [32, 32] | 2 | 41.153 | 16.744 | **2.46×**
bf16 | [128, 64] | 4 | 68.079 | 35.498 | **1.92×**
bf16 | [256, 256] | 4 | 68.927 | 36.992 | **1.86×**
f32 | [128, 64] | 4 | 64.403 | 34.928 | **1.84×**

title: PR #45836: [xla:gpu] Fine grained control of collectives pipelining
body:
PR #45836: [xla:gpu] Fine grained control of collectives pipelining

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45836

Add a `CollectivePipeliningMode` to control what collective operations instances are allowed to be pipelined:

* `DEFAULT` - default pipelining at given opt level
* `OFF` - no pipelining at all
* `ON` - pipeline all operations that could be pipelined (legacy behavior of `true` flag)
* `EXPLICIT` - only pipeline operations marked with a frontend attribute

Explicit pipelining attribute gives more control to end users (JAX) on what operations are ok to pipeline. Simplified example below shows a very simple case with independent collectives, in practice in JAX users might want to statically unroll a small loop inside a scan loop, and pipelining all iterations of unrolled loop is too aggressive and unnecessary increases the buffer assignment and keeps to many collective operations in flight. 

**IMPORTANT:** legacy boolean flags parsed into `ON` (true) or `DEFAULT`
(false) mode to preserve existing behavior.

### Example

Assuming independent collectives, N iterations, and simplified async all-gather operations, the original loop is:

```
  for i = 0 .. N-1:
    a0 = all-gather(x0[i])
    a1 = all-gather(x1[i])
    a2 = all-gather(x2[i])
    compute(i, a0, a1, a2)
```

#### Pipelining all three

All three collectives are prefetched one iteration ahead:

```
  # Prologue: initiate iteration 0 collectives.
  p0 = all-gather-start(x0[0])
  p1 = all-gather-start(x1[0])
  p2 = all-gather-start(x2[0])

  # Steady state.
  for i = 0 .. N-2:
    a0 = all-gather-done(p0)
    a1 = all-gather-done(p1)
    a2 = all-gather-done(p2)

    # Initiate collectives for the next iteration.
    p0 = all-gather-start(x0[i + 1])
    p1 = all-gather-start(x1[i + 1])
    p2 = all-gather-start(x2[i + 1])

    # Ideally overlaps with the next collectives.
    compute(i, a0, a1, a2)

  # Epilogue: consume the final prefetched values.
  a0 = all-gather-done(p0)
  a1 = all-gather-done(p1)
  a2 = all-gather-done(p2)
  compute(N - 1, a0, a1, a2)
```

The loop carries three outstanding collective handles and needs prologue/epilogue plumbing for all three.

#### Pipelining only all-gather-0

In explicit mode:

```
  all-gather-0, is_pipelineable=true
  all-gather-1
  all-gather-2
```

Conceptually becomes:

```
  # Prologue.
  p0 = all-gather-start(x0[0])

  # Steady state.
  for i = 0 .. N-2:
    a0 = all-gather-done(p0)

    # These remain in their original iteration.
    a1 = all-gather(x1[i])
    a2 = all-gather(x2[i])

    # Only all-gather-0 is prefetched.
    p0 = all-gather-start(x0[i + 1])

    compute(i, a0, a1, a2)

  # Epilogue.
  a0 = all-gather-done(p0)
  a1 = all-gather(x1[N - 1])
  a2 = all-gather(x2[N - 1])
  compute(N - 1, a0, a1, a2)
```

Only one collective crosses the iteration boundary, so the loop carries one additional handle instead of three. This reduces loop state, buffering, code-size growth, and the number of outstanding communications.

title: PR #45954: [XLA:GPU][oneAPI] Enable PJRT_Client_DmaMap for SYCL
body:
PR #45954: [XLA:GPU][oneAPI] Enable PJRT_Client_DmaMap for SYCL

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45954

📝 Summary of Changes
Adding support for DMA Map for Intel GPUs. DPC++ exposes the necessary functions (https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/experimental/sycl_ext_oneapi_copy_optimize.asciidoc) to (un)register pinned memory since Jul 2023 (https://github.com/intel/llvm/commit/65cc0cf) and Level zero exposes the relevant functions since the 22.16.22992 release (https://github.com/intel/compute-runtime/commit/9f79e432bb229915e018dda37f8726986aa336f5).

I'm adding the necessary guards just in case with `SYCL_EXT_ONEAPI_COPY_OPTIMIZE` for DPC++. And I'm double-checking with `zexDriverGetHostPointerBaseAddress` if it's present to ensure the registration does succeed as DPC++ will silently fail otherwise.

I've tested this change on a b70 with latest drivers.

🎯 Justification
Allows the use of DmaMap on Intel GPU.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
⚡️ Performance Improvement ✨ New Feature

When a replicated result dynamically slices a single layer from an operand sharded along the layer dimension, XLA previously materialized the full operand with an all-gather and then sliced out the requested layer. This PR lowers that pattern to a per-owner `collective-broadcast`: each partition slices its local candidate, a conditional selects the partition that owns the requested layer, and that owner broadcasts only the selected slice.

## Workload

The motivating workload is Layered-FSDP for Muon.

Muon's Newton-Schulz update needs the full weight/gradient matrix for each layer. To preserve full matrices locally, Layered-FSDP shards scanned layer stacks along the layer dimension instead of sharding the matrix row/column dimensions.

A representative weight layout is:

```text
logical shape: [L, K, N]
sharding:      P("lp", None, None)
```

where `L` is the scanned layer dimension and `lp` is the layer-parallel mesh axis.

During the forward pass, the scan body selects the current layer:

```text
W_i = dynamic-slice(W, i, 0, 0), dynamic_slice_sizes={1, K, N}
```

The selected `W_i` is needed replicated across the LP partitions for the layer computation. If `L == LP`, layer `i` is owned by LP partition `i`.

The ideal communication pattern for scan iteration `i` is therefore:

```text
owner = partition that owns layer i
broadcast W_i from owner to all LP partitions
```

## Original Issue

Before this PR, XLA SPMD did not have a specialized lowering for this case:

```text
replicated result = dynamic-slice(tiled operand, dynamic layer index)
```

Because the operand is sharded on the sliced dimension but the dynamic-slice result is replicated, the existing path falls back to replicating the operand first. In practice this produces:

```text
all-gather full W across LP
dynamic-slice W_i from the gathered W
```

That is correct, but inefficient for this workload.

For example, if the scan only needs one layer's weight `[1, K, N]`, the old lowering gathers the full layer stack `[L, K, N]` and then slices out one layer. This defeats the purpose of Layered-FSDP's layerwise ownership for the forward pass, because every scan iteration communicates all layer shards instead of the one layer needed by that iteration.

## Solution In This PR

This PR adds `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::TryDynamicSliceWithCollectiveBroadcast` and calls it from `HandleDynamicSlice` before the generic replicated-output fallback.

The new lowering matches a conservative pattern:

```text
- dynamic-slice output is replicated
- operand is tiled
- exactly one dimension is dynamically sliced
- sliced size is 1
- operand is sharded only along the sliced dimension
- no partial replication
- partitioning is even
- slice index is an S32 scalar
- operand sharding uses the same number of devices as the SPMD partition count
```

For the matched case, XLA lowers:

```text
dynamic-slice(tiled_operand, i) -> replicated result
```

to:

```text
clamped_i   = clamp(i, 0, dim_size - 1)
owner       = clamped_i / shard_size
local_i     = clamped_i - owner * shard_size
local_slice = dynamic-slice(local_operand, local_i)

result = conditional(owner)
  branch 0: collective-broadcast(local_slice), root=partition owning shard 0
  branch 1: collective-broadcast(local_slice), root=partition owning shard 1
  ...
```

Each conditional branch contains a `collective-broadcast` with a static root. The dynamic part is only the branch selection, which is derived from the replicated layer index. This lets the HLO represent the desired "changing owner per scan iteration" pattern without requiring a dynamic-root collective.

The generated communication now moves only the selected layer slice instead of all layer shards.

## Before / After

Before:

```text
all-gather W_local -> W_full
dynamic-slice W_full[i]
```

After:

```text
local dynamic-slice W_local[local_i]
conditional(owner)
  collective-broadcast from owner partition
```

So the forward pass communication changes from:

```text
communicate [L, K, N] per scan iteration
```

to:

```text
communicate [1, K, N] per scan iteration
```

for the matched Layered-FSDP pattern.

## Testing

Added a focused SPMD partitioner test:

```text
DynamicSliceReplicatedResultUsesCollectiveBroadcast
```

The test verifies that a replicated dynamic-slice result from a layer-sharded operand produces:

```text
- no all-gather
- one conditional with one branch per owner partition
- collective-broadcast in each branch
- replica groups whose first member is the branch's broadcast root
```

Validation performed for the motivating workload:

```text
bazel test --test_output=errors \
  --test_filter="DynamicSliceReplicatedResultUsesCollectiveBroadcast" \
  //xla/service/spmd:spmd_partitioner_test
```

Additional workload validation:

```text
- Rebuilt JAX/JAXLIB CUDA artifacts against this XLA checkout.
- Ran lp_fsdp_muon_test.py --mode lp --no-run --dump-hlo with
  JAX_ENABLE_COMPILATION_CACHE=false.
- Confirmed the LP forward HLO contains the expected conditional
  collective-broadcast lowering.
```

Observed HLO counts for the workload:

```text

collective-broadcast-done  = 32
conditional                = 4
dynamic_slice_collective_broadcast_owner = 16
all-gather-start           = 0
all-gather-done            = 0
```

title: PR #45821: [HLO] Validate the dimensions attribute in the HLO parser to avoid crashes
body:
PR #45821: [HLO] Validate the dimensions attribute in the HLO parser to avoid crashes

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45821

### Problem
Several opcode handlers extract or use a value from the `dimensions={...}` attribute without validating it, so malformed-but-lexable HLO text crashes the parser (a `std::out_of_range` throw, an out-of-bounds read, or a `CHECK`-fail) instead of returning an error `Status`.

**Empty `dimensions={}`** — `all-gather`, `all-gather-start`, `reduce-scatter`, and `get-dimension-size` / `set-dimension-size` extract `dimensions->at(0)`, but the parser only checks that the required attribute is *present*, not non-empty. An empty list therefore throws `std::out_of_range`:
```
all-gather(input), replica_groups={}, dimensions={}
reduce-scatter(input), replica_groups={}, to_apply=add, dimensions={}
get-dimension-size(p), dimensions={}
```

**Out-of-range dimension value** — `scan` checks `dimensions->size() == 1` but then uses the value as `operands[0]->shape().dimensions(scan_dim)` with no range check, so an out-of-range value reads out of bounds (and the downstream `ShapeUtil::InsertDimensionAtIndex` `CHECK`-fails):
```
scan(input, init), dimensions={-1}, num_carries=0, to_apply=add
```

### Fix
- Require `dimensions->size() == 1` in the all-gather / reduce-scatter / get-dimension-size / set-dimension-size handlers before extracting `dimensions->at(0)`, matching the checks the sibling `kSort` and `kAllToAll` handlers already have. (`all-reduce`/`all-reduce-start` share the reduce-scatter parse block and don't take a `dimensions` attribute, so the new check is guarded by `opcode == kReduceScatter`.)
- Range-check `scan`'s dimension against the operand rank and return a parse error if it is out of range.

### Tests
Four `HloParserTest` cases assert that `all-gather`, `reduce-scatter`, and `get-dimension-size` with `dimensions={}`, and `scan` with an out-of-range dimension, now return an error instead of crashing.

---
Disclosure: this contribution was authored with an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed before submission.

title: Fix iterator invalidation in LegalizeSchedulingAnnotations
body:
Fix iterator invalidation in LegalizeSchedulingAnnotations

Use absl::erase_if when removing trivial scheduling groups to prevent map
mutation during range-based for loop iteration. Previously, calling
map.erase() inside a range-for loop over comp_inst_vector and
annotation_to_instruction invalidated iterators and caused assertion
failures when an annotation group spanned multiple computations.

title: [XLA:GPU] Enable AnnotationStack earlier in CuptiTracer and capture annotations for memset events.
body:
[XLA:GPU] Enable AnnotationStack earlier in CuptiTracer and capture annotations for memset events.

Otherwise the line may have the events without annotation_id. As a result of that the entire line will be marked as CUPTI Overhead.

The AnnotationStack is now enabled before API tracing begins, ensuring all API calls are potentially annotated. The AnnotationStack is also disabled if API or activity tracing fails to initialize. Memset events now include associated annotation, NVTX range, and scope range ID looked up from the AnnotationMap.

title: PR #45082: [XLA:GPU] Use packed storage shapes for FP4 XTile operands
body:
PR #45082: [XLA:GPU] Use packed storage shapes for FP4 XTile operands

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45082

📝 Summary of Changes
Update XTile codegen to model packed FP4 scaled-dot operands using their physical storage shape and storage element type. For packed f4E2M1FN operands, XTile now uses i8 storage, divides the packed layout-minor dimension by the number of FP4 elements per byte, adjusts tile offsets for the packed storage coordinate system, and validates that packed tiles use unit stride and byte-aligned offsets. This is the second PR in the decomposition of the larger scaled-dot fix series: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44223.

🎯 Justification
FP4 scaled-dot operands are stored packed: two logical f4E2M1FN values live in one byte. After https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44885, XTile can carry the logical dot element type separately from the tensor storage type. This PR makes the tile and memref storage side consistent with that contract.

This cannot be delayed until Triton lowering because XTile already materializes memref types, tile shapes, slice offsets, and extract geometry before Triton sees the operation. If XTile keeps using logical FP4 shapes at that layer, it can describe incorrect byte storage shapes, tile sizes, and offsets for packed FP4 data. This matters for NVFP4/MXFP4 scaled-dot workloads lowered through Triton, where Triton expects e2m1 operands to be carried as packed i8 storage.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

🧪 Unit Tests:
TritonDevicelessTest.RejectsPackedFp4OddMinorOffset verifies that packed FP4 tiles reject byte-unaligned minor offsets.
TritonDevicelessTest.EmitsPackedFp4StorageForEvenMinorOffset verifies that byte-aligned packed FP4 operands use packed i8 memrefs/tensors, storage-coordinate offsets, and dot_scaled i8 storage element types.

title: PR #45597: [XLA:GPU] Add SKIP_PROFILED command buffer update mode
body:
PR #45597: [XLA:GPU] Add SKIP_PROFILED command buffer update mode

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45597

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This PR adds the `SKIP_PROFILED` command-buffer update mode. The mode
automatically includes command-buffer-referenced preallocated temp allocations
in the final VA-remap set while profiling other eligible non-constant
allocations during the first three successful executions. Stable profile
candidates are combined with the temp allocations so subsequent command-buffer
executions can treat the final set as persistent and avoid unnecessary address
updates.

- Adds `DebugOptions::SKIP_PROFILED` and routes it through the GPU executable
  buffer-allocation policy.
- Adds a per-executor profile state machine to
  `GpuExecutableVaRemapAllocator`: `kProfiling` transitions exactly once to
  `kActive` when an automatic temp or safe profile candidate exists, or to
  `kDisabled` when the final remap set is empty.
- Automatically selects preallocated temp buffers and profiles eligible
  parameter and live-out candidates while filtering unstable addresses,
  non-VMM-backed parameters, and incompatible shared parameter buffers.
- Counts only successful executions toward the profiling window and passes
  `std::nullopt` for persistent allocation indices while profiling, followed by
  one absent-to-present transition to the final persistent set.
- Uses the parameter-remapping support from #45595 and output-buffer remapping
  support from #45596. Parameters and outputs remain externally owned in the
  const owning allocation table; finalized external addresses are mapped into
  an execution-only allocation-table copy immediately before execution.
- Preserves the base allocator fallback when VMM remapping is unavailable or
  there are neither automatic temp buffers nor stable profile candidates.

This PR is stacked on #45596, **[XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of output buffer
allocations**. It is part 3 of 3 and, together with #45595 and #45596,
supersedes the closed pre-split PR #45568.

## 🎯 Justification

`SKIP_TEMP` can stabilize preallocated temporary buffers, but parameters and
live-out buffers may also keep stable physical addresses across repeated
executions. Updating command-buffer node addresses for those stable allocations
adds avoidable runtime overhead.

`SKIP_PROFILED` discovers address stability for each executable/executor pair
instead of assuming every dynamic allocation is stable. Workloads with
repeatable allocation behavior can therefore stabilize more
command-buffer-visible addresses, while unstable or unsupported workloads retain
the existing fallback behavior. Mapping finalized owning addresses immediately
before execution also keeps donation and copy-protection changes compatible with
the const owning-allocation API introduced by the lower PRs.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

No benchmark result is claimed in this draft. The PR adds the policy and
correctness coverage; a public-HLO performance benchmark can be added separately
when reporting workload-specific speedups.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- Extended `GpuExecutableTest.CommandBufferAllocationPolicy` expectations for
  automatic temp-buffer selection in `SKIP_PROFILED`.
- Added host-only fake-VMM coverage for profiling, transition, active remapping,
  and disabled fallback states.
- Verifies a temp-only executable transitions to an active persistent temp set,
  and an unstable parameter cannot disqualify an automatically selected temp.
- Verifies stable parameter and output selection, including non-granularity-sized
  externally owned outputs.
- Verifies failed executions do not advance the three-successful-execution
  profiling window.
- Verifies fallback for unstable and non-VMM-backed parameters and incompatible
  shared parameter buffers.
- Verifies copy protection both during profiling and after transition: the
  owning table retains the finalized external address while execution uses the
  stable reservation address.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

- Added one-device `VmmTest` coverage using a two-GEMM command-buffer workload
  across profiling, transition, and remapped executions, checking numerical
  correctness on every run.
- Verifies one-time profile selection, automatic temp inclusion, VA-reservation
  creation and reuse, and successful deallocation of externally returned output
  buffers.
- Added a non-VMM allocator execution test verifying the workload remains
  correct and creates no VA reservation when remapping is unavailable.

The per-executor profile transitions once from profiling to active or disabled, preserving the required absent-to-present persistent-index transition. - Uses the parameter-remapping support from #45595 and output-buffer remapping
  support from #45596. Parameters and outputs remain externally owned in the
  const owning allocation table; finalized external addresses are mapped into
  an execution-only allocation-table copy immediately before execution.
- Preserves the base allocator fallback when VMM remapping is unavailable or
  there are neither automatic temp buffers nor stable profile candidates.

This PR is stacked on #45596, **[XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of output buffer
allocations**. It is part 3 of 3 and, together with #45595 and #45596,
supersedes the closed pre-split PR #45568.

## 🎯 Justification

`SKIP_TEMP` can stabilize preallocated temporary buffers, but parameters and
live-out buffers may also keep stable physical addresses across repeated
executions. Updating command-buffer node addresses for those stable allocations
adds avoidable runtime overhead.

`SKIP_PROFILED` discovers address stability for each executable/executor pair
instead of assuming every dynamic allocation is stable. Workloads with
repeatable allocation behavior can therefore stabilize more
command-buffer-visible addresses, while unstable or unsupported workloads retain
the existing fallback behavior. Mapping finalized owning addresses immediately
before execution also keeps donation and copy-protection changes compatible with
the const owning-allocation API introduced by the lower PRs.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

No benchmark result is claimed in this draft. The PR adds the policy and
correctness coverage; a public-HLO performance benchmark can be added separately
when reporting workload-specific speedups.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- Extended `GpuExecutableTest.CommandBufferAllocationPolicy` expectations for
  automatic temp-buffer selection in `SKIP_PROFILED`.
- Added host-only fake-VMM coverage for profiling, transition, active remapping,
  and disabled fallback states.
- Verifies a temp-only executable transitions to an active persistent temp set,
  and an unstable parameter cannot disqualify an automatically selected temp.
- Verifies stable parameter and output selection, including non-granularity-sized
  externally owned outputs.
- Verifies failed executions do not advance the three-successful-execution
  profiling window.
- Verifies fallback for unstable and non-VMM-backed parameters and incompatible
  shared parameter buffers.
- Verifies copy protection both during profiling and after transition: the
  owning table retains the finalized external address while execution uses the
  stable reservation address.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

- Added one-device `VmmTest` coverage using a two-GEMM command-buffer workload
  across profiling, transition, and remapped executions, checking numerical
  correctness on every run.
- Verifies one-time profile selection, automatic temp inclusion, VA-reservation
  creation and reuse, and successful deallocation of externally returned output
  buffers.

  correct and creates no VA reservation when remapping is unavailable.

title: PR #44653: Validate buffer slices during deserialization
body:
PR #44653: Validate buffer slices during deserialization

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44653

## Summary

- validate `BufferAllocation::Slice::FromProto` rejects negative offsets and sizes
- reject serialized slices whose `[offset, offset + size)` range exceeds the referenced allocation
- add regression coverage for malformed `BufferAllocationSliceProto` values

## Why

`BufferAllocation::Slice::FromProto` reconstructs runtime buffer slices from serialized executable data. It previously validated only `buffer_allocation_index`, while the compile-time assignment path guarantees that `offset >= 0`, `size >= 0`, and `offset + size <= allocation.size()`. This change enforces that same invariant before constructing the slice.

## Testing

- `git diff --check`
- `clang++ -std=c++17 -fsanitize=address -g -DNDEBUG -DAPPLY_FIX poc_primitive_asan.cc -o /tmp/openxla_poc_fixed && /tmp/openxla_poc_fixed` from the local reproduction bundle; the fixed logic rejects the malformed slice
- attempted `bazel test //xla/service:buffer_assignment_test`; local sparse-checkout setup initially missed top-level `third_party` and `tools`, and after adding them the invocation stayed in Bazel repository mapping until interrupted. Retrying with `--noexperimental_repo_remote_exec` fails during repository initialization because `rules_ml_toolchain` requires that experimental flag.

title: PR #45682: pjrt: propagate Prepare failure on non-two-phase multi-device Execute
body:
PR #45682: pjrt: propagate Prepare failure on non-two-phase multi-device Execute

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45682

## The bug

`CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute`'s multi-device path calls `ExecutePrepareWithOomRetries` per device, then — only when `supports_two_phase_launch()` is true — checks the returned status inside the two-phase barrier block. `CpuClient` overrides `supports_two_phase_launch()` to `false`, so on a multi-device CpuClient a Prepare failure is never checked and execution falls through to `ExecuteLaunch(*launch_args, ...)` with `launch_args.executable` still null → null-deref crash instead of a clean error.

## The fix

Add an `else if (!launch_status.ok())` branch after the two-phase block: record the failure in `results[i]`, decrement `launching` under `mu`, return. Same shape as the two-phase failure path minus the barrier it doesn't participate in.

## Scope

`CpuClient` is the only in-tree client with `supports_two_phase_launch()==false`. Two-phase clients (GPU/TPU stream-executor) are unchanged — the diff is purely additive.

## Test

`MultiDevicePrepareFailurePropagatesError` in `[cpu_client_test.cc](http://cpu_client_test.cc/)`: 2-device CpuClient, 2-replica identity program, wrong-size buffer on device 1 so `CheckBufferCompatibilities` rejects it during Prepare. Asserts `Execute()` returns an error (not a crash) and that the error comes from the per-device Prepare path.

title: PR #45684: pjrt_c_api_gpu: plumb max_inflight_computations through PJRT C-API create options
body:
PR #45684: pjrt_c_api_gpu: plumb max_inflight_computations through PJRT C-API create options

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45684

b261c3b677 ("Respect `GpuOptions::max_inflight_computations` in SE GPU") added `GpuClientOptions::max_inflight_computations` and wired it through the StreamExecutor GPU client, but did not add the corresponding key to the GPU PJRT C API plugin's create-options allowlist. Since `ValidateCreateOptions` rejects unrecognized keys, passing `"max_inflight_computations"` via the plugin path (e.g. JAX's `jax_pjrt_client_create_options`) fails client creation with `Unexpected option name passed to PJRT_Client_Create`, so the field can't be set from Python.

This PR adds the key to `kExpectedOptionNameAndTypes` and forwards it to `GpuClientOptions`. The value is validated to be in `(0, INT32_MAX]`: the field is `int`, and a zero value would construct a compute semaphore that blocks forever on the first `Execute()`. When the option is omitted, the `GpuClientOptions` default (32) is preserved; disabling the semaphore entirely (`std::nullopt`) remains C++-only, since expressing "no limit" through an int64 option would need a sentinel value.

This is GPU-specific because `"max_inflight_computations"` is already among the TPU plugin's published create-option names (`pjrt::tpu_configs::kMaxInflightComputations`, `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_tpu_constants.h`); this change brings the GPU plugin to parity.

Tested: `pjrt_c_api_gpu_test` — `PjrtCApiGpuMaxInflightComputationsTest.{Valid,Invalid}OptionsParsing`.

97d9700e399566f6c986216c55078ec94de54d5b by Nikhil Bhargava <nikhil@anthropic.com>:

pjrt_c_api_gpu: plumb max_inflight_computations through PJRT C-API create options

Adds "max_inflight_computations" to the PJRT_Client_Create options dict so
GpuClientOptions.max_inflight_computations is settable from Python via the
plugin options (e.g. jax_plugins.cuda.initialize()). The value is validated
to be in (0, INT32_MAX]; out-of-range values return InvalidArgument rather
than silently producing a zero-capacity compute semaphore that deadlocks at
first Execute().

b261c3b677 plumbed max_inflight_computations through GpuClientOptions, but
the PJRT C API layer doesn't yet accept it from the create-options dict, so
there's no way to set it from Python. This closes that gap.

title: PR #45596: [XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of output buffer allocations
body:
PR #45596: [XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of output buffer allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45596

## 📝 Summary of Changes

This PR extends command-buffer virtual-address remapping to allocations that
escape to the caller (`maybe_live_out`) while preserving the const ownership
model introduced by #45595.

- Keeps selected live-out allocations at normal allocator-owned addresses in
  the owning `BufferAllocations` table.
- Extends `GetRemappedBufferAllocations` to map finalized selected input/output
  addresses into their stable reservation slices immediately before execution.
- Rewrites only the non-owning execution copy, so result handling and teardown
  continue to see external, deallocatable addresses.
- Handles donated and copy-protected aliases by mapping after output setup has
  finalized the owning address table.
- Extends the host-only fake-VMM tests to cover stable execution aliases,
  logical external sizes, output deallocation, and deferred alias cleanup.

This PR is stacked on #45595, **[XLA:GPU] Support VA remapping of parameter
buffer allocations**. It is part 2 of 3 splitting the former #45568
implementation; #45597 adds the `SKIP_PROFILED` mode.

## 🎯 Justification

Live-out buffers can outlive an execution scope, so the caller must retain a
normal allocator-owned address that remains valid and can be passed to
`Deallocate()`. At the same time, recorded command buffers need a stable
reservation address.

Building a separate execution allocation table provides both properties
without mutating the owning table or removing its const qualifier. Deferring
the mapping until execution also ensures donation and copy protection have
already selected the final external address.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable as a standalone change. This PR adds output-buffer remapping
support but does not independently enable a new command-buffer update mode.
Performance evaluation belongs to the final `SKIP_PROFILED` policy in #45597.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- Extends the host-only fake-VMM allocator test with a non-granularity-aligned
  remapped live-out allocation.
- Verifies the owning table contains the logical-size external address before
  and after execution.
- Verifies execution receives the same stable reservation address across runs
  and maps the correct raw physical allocation.
- Verifies the external address is deallocatable and all aliases are released.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

No standalone execution test is added for this enabling layer. End-to-end
live-out selection, execution, and output deallocation are covered by the
stacked `SKIP_PROFILED` change in #45597.

This preserves const ownership semantics, handles donation and copy protection before mapping, and leaves output addresses deallocatable by callers.
